latest_substantive_result.summary: The selected unit preserves two distinct source-reported results for a specified overdamped diffusion. First, a static Poisson/Laplace argument gives an ordered-limit existence result: for sufficiently large finite H, then sufficiently small finite frequency and amplitude, the full continuous field port can receive work. This is not a result at the separately fixed H=12, A=0.3, slow-frequency 0.01 waveform. Second, six floating finite-volume resolutions at that fixed waveform report field-port work around -7.4e-4 per cycle, while the maintained-force input is about +3.739, so the two controls still supply net work to the medium. No certified PDE error enclosure, physical result, efficiency, practical advantage or novelty is established.

next_decisive_step: No follow-up work is implied. Any future fixed-waveform claim would need a certified full-period PDE error enclosure and force/current convergence; any physical claim would additionally need finite-H constitutive calibration, preparation, actuator and maintained-force accounting. This intake does not resume that work.

limitations: The ordered-limit proof is source-reported. This integration did not rederive or independently certify it; the supplied review had prior exposure to the finite construction and did not replay code.

The ordered-limit choices of H, frequency and amplitude do not establish negative work at H=12, A=0.3 and slow frequency 0.01; the source supplies no quantified fixed-H interval or uniform-in-H remainder.

The H=12 full-cycle result is floating finite-volume evidence over six refinements, not a certified PDE mesh-error enclosure. The force/heat ledger remains spatially unconverged at the reported precision.
At the finest listed resolution the field port returns about 0.000744608 work units per cycle but the maintained-force input is about 3.739017; the two controls still supply net work to the medium.

Four warm-up cycles from a uniform numerical start do not establish a free or physically available periodic-state preparation. Controller, force source, sensing, phase synchronization and hardware losses are not acquired or priced.

The model stipulates overdamped white-noise dynamics. Barrier height/restoring force grow with H, and finite mass/bath memory may violate that constitutive assumption at high H; finite-H physical calibration is absent.
Power and output/fuel ratio vanish along the stated slow/small-amplitude existence choices. No efficient engine, useful power, physical observation, practical advantage or novelty is established.

A continuum well is not an exact single microscopic state. The discrete atomic-return test does not transfer; a continuous hitting-time protocol would have distinct synchronization and monitoring costs.

The broad source-clock closed-cycle Gibbs-tilt derivation from the earlier kinetic unit remains unresolved. Neither the continuous existence argument nor the fixed-H numerical report closes it; N713 and its open review gate are unchanged.
